You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

<sentences>
S1: He reports an onset of a few months ago but denies any specific injury.
S2: After reviewing the patient's clinical history and examination today, I have had a lengthy discussion with him regarding treatment options for his current symptoms.
S3: NEURO: Decreased sensation in the right thumb and index finger.
S4: His symptoms are worse at night, and he wakes with numbness in the bilateral hands.
S5: He experiences numbness in all fingers, but states it is the most noticeable in the left thumb and index finger.
S6: George Lewis is a pleasant 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of left wrist and hand pain.
S7: He reports he drops objects and explains “I have a hard time feeling it.”
S8: The patient will follow up with me in 2 weeks when the EMG results are available for review.
S9: The patient denies a history of rheumatoid arthritis.
S10: However, the patient notes he often engages in repetitive motions while performing his work duties.
S11: I advised him to take ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours.
S12: Musculoskeletal: Reports left wrist and hand pain.
S13: Left wrist and hand pain.
S14: For relief, he shakes his hands upon waking.
S15: Positive Tinel sign bilaterally.
S16: The patient also experiences weakness in his left hand.
S17: Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome.
S18: I also recommended that he wear a wrist splint to provide increased support.
S19: If at that time his symptoms have not improved with these conservative measures, we will discuss further treatment options including additional diagnostic testing or possible surgical intervention.
S20: He affirms intermittent numbness in the left little finger.
S21: Denies right hand pain.
S22: Additionally, I recommended we obtain an EMG of the bilateral upper extremities to evaluate for carpal tunnel syndrome.
S23: MSK: Examination of the bilateral hands: Grip strength is less on the left in comparison to the right.
S24: The patient states he understands and is in agreement with the plan.
S25: He reports consuming 1 to 2 beers on weekends.
S26: All questions were answered to the patient's satisfaction.
S27: The patient will follow up with me in 2 weeks.
S28: Neurological: Reports numbness in bilateral hands and fingers, and left hand weakness.
S29: He works in landscaping.
S30: I discussed the importance of activity modification and encouraged the patient to limit active repetitive motions while working for the next 2 weeks.
</sentences>
